subject: Pen testing SOWs - three vendor proposals & split-scope options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Pen testing SOWs - three vendor proposals & split-scope options

Team —

Attached are the three vendor proposals we received for this year's offensive testing: RedShield, PenTestCo, and AtlasSecurity. Procurement asked I get alignment on scope before they open a PO. Key constraints from infra/ops are below; please reply with your top choice and any absolute no-go items by EOD Monday.

Summary (high level):
- RedShield Labs: full-scope red team + tailored scoping for cloud infra. Higher cost, flexible windows, promises simulated social engineering. SOW v3 attached.
- PenTestCo: focused application penetration testing (web/mobile) + static analysis integration workshop. Mid cost, faster turnaround. Scope matrix attached.
- AtlasSecurity: retainer-style continuous testing + prioritized regression re-tests. Lower hourly rate but longer engagement. Quote attached.

Operational asks for your input:
1) Do we want a single vendor to handle both appsec and red team, or split (appsec: PenTestCo, red team: RedShield)?
2) Preferred testing windows: we can do a split window (app tests in Oct, red team in Nov) to limit risk to deployments.
3) Evidence handoff: all vendors propose different artifact formats (PDF reports vs aggregated findings feed). We prefer machine-readable results to feed the vuln tracker.

Attachments: [RedShield_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 42 pages)], [PenTestCo_scope_matrix.xlsx], [AtlasSecurity_quote.pdf]

Notes: legal will likely push back on social engineering add-ons and any presigned consent scope; Laura, please advise on must-have contract clauses. Marcus, please confirm whether we can support a two-week staging window for the red team without disrupting the release schedule. Mina, procurement asks for preferred vendor order to use in the PO.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen testing SOWs - three vendor proposals & split-scope options

Vivek — quick notes after skimming the three:

RedShield:
- Pros: deep red-team experience, includes social engineering playbook and post-engagement retest window.
- Cons: price is high and their evidence is mainly narrative + screenshots; we need CSV/JSON exports for our tracker. Vendor said they can add a feed but there will be a cost line.

PenTestCo:
- Pros: good appsec coverage and they include a pipeline-integrated SCA/SAST handoff. Their scope matrix maps cleanly to our sprint cadence.
- Cons: no social engineering or physical tests.

AtlasSecurity:
- Pros: lower hourly, ongoing retainer model which could be useful for quarterly checks.
- Cons: turn-around on remediation verification is slow; may not suit a tight release calendar.

My recommendation: split scope. Use PenTestCo for focused appsec testing (fast, integrates with pipeline) and RedShield for a single focused red-team engagement (includes phishing/social engineering). Atlas could be retained for lower-cost quarterly checks, but not for this cycle.

Also: procurement asked if we can accept a staged delivery: initial exec summary + machine-readable vuln dump within 5 business days of report. If yes, I'll ask vendors to include that as an acceptance criterion.

Best,
Mina
Senior Security Program Manager

[attachment: PenTestCo_scope_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)]
From: RedShield Labs <contracts@redshieldlabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SOW clarifications for Redwood Inference

Vivek / Team —

Appreciate the opportunity to bid. A few clarifications based on Mina's note:
- We can provide machine-readable findings (JSON export) as an add-on; estimate: +$3,500.
- Social engineering elements (phishing) will require written consent from the C-suite and a narrow target list. We will run a separate briefing and opt-in form.
- We can split the engagement into a 10-business-day reconnaissance + 5-business-day active exercise window. If you prefer split months (Oct/Nov), we can accommodate that.

Attached: RedShield_SOW_v3.pdf (redacted PII)

Regards,
Contracts Team
RedShield Labs
[attachment: RedShield_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 42 pages)]

From: RedShield Sales <sales@redshieldlabs.com>
To: contracts@redshieldlabs.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood RFP notes

(Internal vendor notes forwarded for our record)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen testing SOWs - three vendor proposals & split-scope options

Vivek / team —

Legal comments (high level):
- No vendor should be authorized to perform social engineering without a signed targeted consent addendum; we will provide an addendum template.
- Indemnity cap: propose $1M for offensive engagements; vendors are pushing back — procurement to escalate if they insist on lower limits.
- Data handling: require machine-readable findings to be delivered over SFTP (or secure API) and retained for 90 days. No persistent copies in vendor-run Google Drive.
- SLA on remediation verification: include 10-business-day verification window once a patch is deployed.

Please loop legal early if RedShield insists on broad authority for user-targeted tests. Also confirm whether we will require background checks / NDAs for any vendor operators with sensitive access.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen testing SOWs - three vendor proposals & split-scope options

Quick ops constraints from Engineering:
- We cannot have a red-team active window that overlaps the sprint release on Oct 29 - Nov 2. That week is feature freeze.
- Staging environment: we can provision isolated staging for appsec work Oct 11-22. Production-affecting tests must be limited to the Nov 8-12 window (after the release).
- We prefer PenTestCo to do app tests during the Oct window; they can integrate findings into CI. RedShield can run their active exercise Nov 8-12.

On evidence format: JSON export to SFTP is ideal. We will provide a temporary account if procurement/legal sign off on access controls.

If procurement wants to split PO lines, we should do: PenTestCo (appsec) first; RedShield (red team) second; Atlas as optional retainer.

-Marcus
Engineering Manager, Platform

[inline: snippet of staging availability calendar]
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.l@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Decision: split-scope approach & next steps for PO

Thanks everyone — consensus captured below. I'm going to ask procurement to proceed with two POs unless legal flags anything urgent.

Final decision (summary):
- PenTestCo: engage for focused application penetration testing during Oct 11-22 (app tests + CI handoff). Ask them to include the machine-readable export option (no cost change expected).
- RedShield Labs: engage for red-team active exercise Nov 8-12 (phased recon + active). RedShield will provide JSON export as an add-on; procurement to negotiate cost. Social engineering will be a separate addendum and requires C-suite sign-off.
- AtlasSecurity: omit from current cycle; ask them for a quarterly-retainer quote for future budgeting.

Action items:
- Mina: consolidate comments and send PenTestCo + RedShield the confirmed windows and required deliverables (json export to SFTP, delivery timelines). Due: Fri 24 Sep.
- Laura: prepare consent addendum template and indemnity negotiation points; share with procurement. Due: Mon 27 Sep.
- Neha / Procurement: open PO # (use po_template.docx), request final vendor invoices and start contract routing in DocuSign. Include budget lines for the JSON export add-on to RedShield. Due: Tue 28 Sep.
- Marcus: prepare ephemeral SFTP account and environment isolation steps; share access steps with vendors once contracts are signed. Due: Nov 1.

Attachments to include in PO packet: [RedShield_SOW_v3.pdf], [PenTestCo_scope_matrix.xlsx], [AtlasSecurity_quote.pdf], [po_template.docx]

If no objections, I'll mark this as approved and notify procurement to proceed.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
